LDEM_80S_20MPP_ADJ.title: LOLA Digital Elevation Model, 80-90 deg S, 20 m/pixel, track-adjusted
LDEM_80S_20MPP_ADJ.publisher: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, Planetary Geodesy Data Archive (PGDA); LRO LOLA team

raster.verified_by: rasterio 1.5.2 / GDAL 3.12.2 header read over HTTP range requests (no bulk download)
raster.registration: pixel-centre samples (GMT node_offset=1; PGDA: X/Y are pixel centres); GeoTIFF origin is the outer pixel edge
raster.units: metres (file history shows a km->m multiplication by 1000)

crs.name: Moon (2015) - Sphere / Ocentric / South Polar (IAU:30135)
crs.projection: Polar_Stereographic, latitude_of_origin=-90, central_meridian=0, false easting/northing 0, metres
crs.scale: No scale_factor parameter present; with latitude_of_origin = -90 the true-scale latitude is the pole (k0=1)
crs.verified_orientation: x = rho*sin(lon_east), y = rho*cos(lon_east), rho = 2R*tan((lat+90deg)/2). Matches pyproj on the file CRS exactly; confirmed by DEM heights at two independently published sites (see height_checks).

LDEM_80S_20MPP_ADJ.height_datum: Metres above the 1737.4 km reference sphere (confirmed against NAIF-published altitudes, same sphere).

frame.stated_by: PGDA landing page text (NOT embedded in the GeoTIFF): 'MOON_ME reference frame of the JPL DE421 ephemeris'.
frame.compatibility_with_planned_ephemeris: NAIF frame kernel moon_de440_250416.tf defines MOON_ME as an alias of MOON_ME_DE440_ME421, a frame 'closely aligned' with DE421's ME frame. NAIF quotes a maximum rotation difference of 3.0709840342771E-07 rad (about 53.4 cm on the surface) over 2000-2040 and 5.82E-07 rad (just over 1 m) over 1900-2051. The generic MOON_PA frame differs from MOON_ME by ~0.02886 deg (~875 m) and MUST NOT be used with this DEM.
frame.requirement: Stage 3 must use the SPICE frame MOON_ME (id 31001, via moon_de440_250416.tf + moon_pa_de440_200625.bpc), never MOON_PA. The residual (<=~1 m) is an uncertainty to be recorded, and its effect checked against Horizons in Stage 3.
frame.not_verified: Whether PGDA's LOLA tie-to-DE421 is exactly MOON_ME_DE421 beyond the product text; the file itself carries no frame metadata.

height_checks.note: recorded during Stage 2 orientation test; reproduced by tests
recorded during Stage 2 orientation test; reproduced by tests

coverage.latitude: Square grid +/-304 km. MEASURED (overview level 5, 1280 m, scripts/verify_dem_product.py): 100% of pixels are finite (no NaN), including the square's corners which reach ~75.9 S. Valid therefore does NOT mean high-quality: data outside the nominal 80-90 S circle and gap-filled areas must be judged with the LDEC/ERR/EFFRES layers (not yet fetched). Treat pixels north of 80 S as unvalidated.
sites_covered: im1-odysseus (80.13 S, only ~0.13 deg = ~4 km inside the edge: unsuitable for horizon work)
im2-athena (84.79 S: ~150 km from the grid edge on its nearest side)
sites_not_covered: chandrayaan3-shiv-shakti (69.37 S): needs a 60S product (e.g. LDEM_60S_240MPP_ADJ / 120MPP / 60MPP), not yet registered

known_limitations: Gridded and interpolated from LOLA altimeter tracks; the LDEC (count) and EFFRES layers must be consulted to judge real resolution (PGDA: ~90% of 5 m pixels in the related 5 m products are interpolated; the equivalent fraction for the 20 m product is not yet measured by us).
Height/slope uncertainty for THIS product is in the _ERR layers, which Stage 2 does not download. PGDA's quoted 0.3-0.5 m RMS applies to the 5 m site products, not to this one.
Overview levels (factor 2-64) are area-averaged (measured, see measurements); averaging lowers peaks, so horizon obstruction from overview data is a lower bound.
Frame information is not embedded in the file (see frame.not_verified).

measurements.overview_resampling_inference: Area-average (not nearest): at IM-2 the overview-3 (320 m) pixel = 5190.37 m; mean of its 16x16 20 m block = 5189.91 m; median 5188.20 m; nearest candidates 5163.42 m / 5193.60 m. Consistent with averaging.
measurements.overview_implication: Averaged overviews smooth ridge peaks, so a horizon computed from them can UNDER-estimate obstruction (optimistic visibility). Far-field use in Stage 4 must quantify this.
